title: Environmental Data Analysis
intro: A one-semester course on turning environmental measurements into defensible answers — sampling design, uncertainty, and reproducible analysis.

add_content_to_page.add_paragraph: This course is built around one dataset that students carry from week one to the final report. We start with the sampling design, move through exploratory analysis and uncertainty, and finish with a reproducible analysis that another person can run.

add_table.heading: At a glance
content_of_rows_separated_by_comma: Assessment, Project report and oral defence

add_list.heading: By the end of the course you can
add_items_to_list: Design a sampling campaign that answers a stated question.
Distinguish measurement error from environmental variation.
Fit and critique a simple mixed-effects model.
Produce an analysis another researcher can rerun from the raw files.
Communicate uncertainty to a non-specialist audience.

items_of_the_timeline.timeline_item_text: From a research question to a sampling plan; pseudoreplication and its costs.
Detection limits, calibration, and propagating error through a calculation.
Fixed and random effects; when a model is more than a line through points.
Project structure, version control and a report that reruns cleanly.

add_special_note.heading: Software
add_special_note.text: We teach in **R**, with RStudio. No prior R experience is assumed, but students who have never written code should budget extra time in the first three weeks.

add_items_to_list: **Project report** — 60%: a full analysis of the course dataset, with code.
**Oral defence** — 25%: 20 minutes, focused on choices and limits.
**Core** — textbook chapters 1–6 and two methodological papers.
**Optional** — one case study from a related field each week.

add_quote.text: An analysis you cannot rerun is an opinion with a chart attached.
